ciphertext_source: Klaus Schmeh, Cipherbrain, 'Update: Five encrypted radio transmissions from a New York Nazi spy' (2021), fetched 24 Sept 2026 (sources/schmeh/posts/47b-koehler-update-2021.txt), reproducing David Kahn, Cryptologia 5:2 (April 1981); transcription, not an image. Message three is headed 137 by Kahn but has 140 letters as printed; message four is headed 140 and has 140.
alphabet: a-z, 26 letters all present, five-letter groups

constraints.sender: Walter Koehler, Dutch, Abwehr agent, FBI double agent in New York from 1942; these five went to Abwehrleitstelle Frankreich, Paris Funkstelle, outside FBI control (Schmeh 2021 after Johnson, Warfare History Network)
constraints.known: the FBI-run channel used a book cipher on a Dutch prayer book (Johnson); these messages were not on that channel
constraints.ic_note: flat IC (cheap test 1, specs/cheap-tests/koehler_ic.out): not a transposition of German or English (controls 0.072 / 0.065); chi-square vs uniform 58.7 on 25 df, so weakly non-uniform (z frequent, c rare)

cheap_test_done: Cheap test 1 (pooled IC), 24 Sept 2026, survey worker (specs/cheap-tests/koehler_ic.py / .out): pooled 924-letter IC 0.0399 vs German plain control 0.0725 / English plain control 0.0645 / uniform-random control 0.0385 (per-message and pooled, 50-window controls each); chi-square vs uniform 58.7 on 25 df (37.7 at p=0.05). Read: flat, not a transposition of German or English; weakly non-uniform (z frequent, c rare).

cheap_tests_in_order[0] (periodic IC / Kasiski, period 2-30), 24 Sept 2026, LANE B breadth worker bKOE (session_0125YSNMcCskE21MtmQTNAFN, Sonnet, cost see ROOM.md/LEDGER): specs/cheap-tests/koehler_periodic.py / .out, per-message coset method (key/shift restarts at each of the 5 message boundaries, not pooled as one stream -- pooling first gave a misaligned, weaker signal, fixed and noted in the script). Target best coset-IC 0.0468 (period 17, seeds 1-3 identical since the target has no randomness); Kasiski finds only 2 repeated-trigram distance pairs total across all 5 messages, no period concentration. Matched controls, same message lengths, German plaintext (tools/data/de16), same method, seeds 1-3: (a) periodic-Vigenere control with a known true period (6, 29, 9 across the 3 seeds) -- coset IC 0.0650-0.0805 at the true period, Kasiski distance pairs (12-37) concentrated on the true period and its divisors; (b) one-time-key control (independent random shift per letter, never repeated) -- coset IC 0.0443-0.0472, no period concentration, matching the target and uniform (~0.0385). Read: this method recovers a real period-2-30 Vigenere-family key on ciphertext this short and design when one is present (control a) and correctly reads flat when one is not (control b); the target reads at control-b/uniform level on both statistics. Not a fixed short-period Vigenere/Beaufort over these five messages for period 2-30; consistent with a one-time key, a code/book system, or a period outside 2-30. No candidate plaintext was produced (a negative on period, not a decode), so tools/judge_plaintext.py was not run. Rules out cheap_tests_in_order item 4 (Vigenere hill-climb) as the next step; items 2/3 (archive lookup, already the spec's next-ranked route) or 5 (book cipher) remain live.
cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Periodic IC / Kasiski on the pooled 924 letters for a period 2-30 (a Vigenère-family or running-key would show one; a one-time pad or a book cipher with word sums would not). Cost under $1, Sonnet.

2. Archive lookup (recovery route): TNA Discovery API for KV 2 files on Walter Koehler / Köhler (the Security Service's double-agent files) and HW 19 (ISOS/ISK decrypts of Abwehr traffic, where a Paris-Funkstelle message of Feb 1944 would have been read by GC&CS); Kahn 1981 cites the TNA letter that quotes the five messages, so start from his footnote. A file that holds the Abwehr's own decrypt ends the item as found-solved. Cost $3-5, Sonnet, one host at a time.
3. FBI Vault / NARA RG 65 'Walter Koehler' for the FBI's later reconstruction (the 1970s journalist's source). Cost $2.

4. If test 1 shows a period: Vigenère/Beaufort hill-climb in de, nl, en judged by tools/judge_plaintext.py; matched control = a German (and a Dutch) plaintext of 924 letters under a random key of the found period, same solver, same restarts (rule 3). Cost $3, Sonnet.

5. If flat: book cipher with letter arithmetic (Thouless-style word sums; Bean's 2019 method ranks candidate key texts by the letter frequencies of the decrypt) over Dutch and German Gutenberg texts. Cost $10-20, strongest model to design, Sonnet to run. Only after 2 and 3 fail.
matched_control: same length and alphabet, German plaintext (tools/data/de16) under the hypothesised system, run before any negative is written
